Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

50 nautical miles
200 nautical miles
350 nautical miles

options: Walker
AMOC
Hadley
Ferrel

mcqs.q: What is the 'race to the bottom' critique of globalisation?
options: Lag time is the delay between thunder and lightning.
Race to the bottom is when companies offshore work to mines and underground factories.
The race to the bottom means TNCs compete with each other for the lowest prices.

The argument that TNCs play countries off against each other, relocating to those with lowest wages, weakest regulation and lowest taxes — pressuring governments to cut standards to attract investment.

mcqs.q: How does an oxbow lake form from a meander?
options: Oxbow lakes form where two rivers meet and one stops flowing.
Oxbow lakes form when meanders dry up completely.
Race to the bottom is when companies offshore work to mines and underground factories.
Erosion on outside bends narrows the meander neck; during a flood the river cuts across the neck, deposition seals the old loop, leaving a horseshoe-shaped lake.

mcqs.q: What is lag time on a storm hydrograph?
options: Lag time is the delay between thunder and lightning.
The time between peak rainfall and peak river discharge — affected by drainage basin shape, land use, soil saturation and vegetation.
Lag time is how long the storm itself lasts.
Oxbow lakes form where two rivers meet and one stops flowing.
